title: Hands — an interactive task-to-result onboarding app
task: Build a beautifully designed, locally runnable interactive website prototype for Hands. This is an app interface, not a marketing landing page. Guide someone through exactly three meaningful stages: give Hands a task, correct it while the demo task is in progress, and inspect a result showing the final task plus applied correction. Make the flow work with real local JavaScript and keyboard controls on desktop and mobile. Keep a short visible 'Interactive prototype' label; it has no live model, microphone or computer-control backend. Use no account credentials, remote services or external assets. Deliver index.html, prototype.css, prototype.js and README.md. Return the finished bundle to Jev to validate, preview and deliver. The prototype must be a polished, useful demonstration whose controls actually change state, not a static mockup or fabricated live session.

creativeBrief.audience: A first-time Hands user trying to understand how to start and steer a task.
creativeBrief.productFacts: Hands is a computer-use assistant project. Its intended interaction is a request, live user correction and a visible result. This local artifact demonstrates that interaction only.
creativeBrief.direction: A warm, precise instrument panel: cream paper, near-black ink, a purposeful cobalt or vermilion accent, fine rules, a confident large task heading and an original abstract hand/gesture motif drawn with CSS or SVG. Use a deliberate app shell and clear state hierarchy. Avoid generic dark gradient SaaS cards, stock imagery, arbitrary pill clutter and long disclaimers. Use local system fonts with considered weight, size and line length. Design all three stages with equal care.
creativeBrief.layout: Desktop around 1440x900 may use a narrow stage rail and spacious main workspace; mobile around 390x844 should make the current stage and primary action immediately understandable. Keep the current task, its latest correction and the result visually distinct. The exact creative composition is the specialist's choice.
creativeBrief.copy: Short, concrete and product-facing. One brief prototype label is sufficient; do not expose provider names, model tokens, runtime provenance or evaluation procedure in the user flow. Put implementation and testing notes in README only.
creativeBrief.motion: Subtle functional feedback for state changes; no long fake loading delays. Honor prefers-reduced-motion. Do not request microphone or browser permissions.

interactionContract.stage1: A labeled task textarea and a few optional example-task buttons. Blank submission is blocked with an accessible explanation. Starting a nonempty task moves to stage2 and preserves the user's exact request as visible text. User input must be escaped; markup-like strings must never execute.
interactionContract.stage2: A visibly simulated in-progress state with a labeled correction textarea. The user can apply a nonempty correction, see an explicit updated-plan representation containing the original task and latest correction, and continue to the result. Empty correction is blocked accessibly. Applying another correction replaces the latest correction while retaining meaningful revision history; do not silently discard it or append duplicate changes. No natural-language interpretation is claimed: reflecting the exact correction is sufficient. Continue only when at least one correction has been applied.
interactionContract.stage3: A clearly labeled preview result that includes the exact original task and latest applied correction, plus a small useful local demonstration artifact or plan. Do not claim real files were generated by an AI or a computer task actually ran. A Back/Edit control returns to the correction stage with values intact. A Reset/New task control returns to an empty initial state and clears result/revision state.
interactionContract.state: Use in-memory state; do not depend on localStorage, cross-origin services or clipboard permissions. Browser reload may reset the demo. Every visible button or link must have a working, meaningful result, with no dead toggles or pretend upload/send controls.
interactionContract.accessibility: Native semantic controls, clear labels, visible keyboard focus, sensible focus movement after stage transitions, aria-live status updates that are not noisy, adequate hit targets and legible contrast. At 390px width there must be no horizontal scroll or trapped primary action.
interactionContract.hosting: The production artifact preview has an opaque origin with sandbox allow-scripts and form-action none. Native form submission is blocked before submit listeners. Use semantic type=button controls plus explicit click handlers for local actions; native Enter/Space on focused buttons works. Do not depend on submit/requestSubmit, allow-forms, storage, clipboard, network or parent-window access. Preserve Enter as newline in textareas.

sourcePolicy: This is a local conceptual product prototype based on the supplied brief. No external factual research is necessary; do not invent remote dependencies or claim that source retrieval proves real product behavior.

mustPass: Actual Hands specialist generation and a fresh Jev return decision save and deliver the completed artifact; a case packet, static screenshot, external coordinator-written site or unexecuted plan does not count.
All four required files are present and locally loadable without external assets, network calls, runtime errors or storage/permission dependencies.
Task input rejects blank content, accepts a preset or custom request and preserves the exact supplied text safely in later stages.
The correction stage is genuinely interactive: reject blank correction, apply and visibly retain a correction, apply a replacement correction, and use the latest correction in the final result.
Result, Back/Edit and Reset/New task controls work; going back preserves current values, while reset clears all task/correction/result state.
All advertised controls are exercised through actual browser interactions. The test includes a task containing markup-like text and confirms it remains inert visible text.

Direct visual inspection at 1440x900 and 390x844 covers all three states. Main task, correction, status and primary action are legible without clipping, overlap, horizontal scrolling or inconsistent spacing.

The composition feels like a purpose-designed product app, with coherent typography, hierarchy, color and iconography; it is not a generic landing page, blank scaffold, arbitrary card grid or copy of the existing personal site.
Keyboard-only navigation reaches and activates the full core flow with visible focus, meaningful labels and usable error/status feedback. Reduced-motion preference removes nonessential motion.
A short prototype label truthfully distinguishes local simulation from real model/computer operation. No invented biography, account, customer, live backend, benchmark or deployment claim appears.
README describes how to open the artifact and the real interaction boundaries. It does not fabricate testing or model provenance; those are recorded by runtime and independent inspection.

inspectionPlan: Exercise empty input, preset task, custom task, first correction, replacement correction, result, back and reset at desktop and mobile sizes.
Capture all three states at each size; directly inspect images and the full below-fold layout.
Run a second keyboard-only flow and inspect focus/labels/errors. Test inert markup-like task text and reduced-motion CSS.
Hash-match inspected files to the Hands manifest. Record measured calls, timing, defects, repairs and any remaining advisories.
